settings.title: Light roles
settings.intro: Every light is main unless you say otherwise. Flow cards can target main or ambient lights separately. Excluded lights are never touched by any card, whatever it targets.

defaults.title: Automatic brightness
defaults.intro: Point each room at the variables that already hold its brightness and temperature. The automatic set-card then carries no values of its own — it reads them here.
defaults.offbelowhint: A brightness this low means off, for every card — not just the automatic one. A circadian variable rarely lands on an exact zero, and a bulb held at 3% is a glow nobody asked for. Set it to 0 to turn lights off only at exactly zero.

daylight.title: Daylight
daylight.intro: Let the light a room already has drive its automatic brightness. Pick where the room reads daylight from, then how it should use it. Rooms left unset behave exactly as before.
daylight.modeshint: Hold a level aims the room at a measured brightness and converges over about twenty minutes, which is what a sensor sitting in the room is actually good for. Follow the daylight moves the mapped brightness between two readings instead — no waiting, but no defined level either. Published figures (300–500 lux on a worktop, 150–300 in a living room) are measured at the task; a ceiling sensor reads a fraction of them, so light the room the way it should look and press Measure rather than typing a number from a table.
daylight.swinghint: How far daylight may move the mapped brightness, up or down. Keep it small: a sensor sitting in the room it lights can otherwise chase its own lamps up and down for hours.
daylight.weatherhint: Modelled daylight is computed from the sun's position and this device's cloud cover — it never sees your lamps, so it cannot chase itself. With no device mapped, or once its reading goes stale, the model falls back to a clear sky rather than to darkness.
daylight.nogeo: Homey has no location set, so modelled daylight cannot be computed.
